title: Your contract at a glance
summary: The main terms of your offer in plain English, including your anchor days.
body:
## Your contract at a glance

This is a plain-English summary of the main terms in your offer. Your signed contract is the full document. If the two ever differ, the signed contract applies.

- **Start date:** shown at the top of your journey
- **Working pattern:** full time (example)
- **Anchor days:** {{anchorDays}}
- **Probation period:** 6 months (example)
- **Notice period:** 1 month (example)

### What are anchor days?

Anchor days are the days each week when your team asks everyone to be in the office together. On other days you choose where you work, as long as you can still do your job well and meet your commitments.

Your LM can talk you through how anchor days work in your team.

### Important

Every figure on this page is an example for this demo. None of it is LBG policy.

### Questions about your contract?

Ask your LM first. If they can't help, use the Teams chat link on the help page to contact People & Places (P&P).

title: Desks, monitors and your workspace
summary: What is at your desk on your first day, and how to ask for a second monitor.
body:
## Your workspace

On your first day you have a desk in your team's area of the office. Floor plans are on the office page.

Desks are bookable. On days you are not on an anchor day you may share a desk with colleagues (example).

### What is at your desk

- A height-adjustable desk (example)
- One monitor as standard, or two if your role needs them
- A docking station for your laptop
- A keyboard and mouse
- A headset for Teams calls

### Asking for a second monitor

Ask your LM. Your LM approves monitor requests and raises the IT request for you (example process).

### Working from home

You can order home working items such as a desk, chair or monitor. The home working order guide explains how.

title: Your devices: laptop, mobile phone and headset
summary: What you can have on day one: a laptop matched to your job family, a mobile phone and a headset. Choose your laptop, then any optional peripherals.
body:
## Your devices on day one

Every colleague can have the following (example entitlements, figures are illustrative):

### Laptop: two tiers, two choices each

Your laptop depends on your **job family**, which comes from your offer. You are offered the two models for your tier and pick one.

**Engineering (high spec)**

- **MacBook Pro M5 Pro** (Mac). A good choice if you already use macOS, or your work needs the most performance.
- **HP EliteBook U7** (Windows). A good choice if you already use Windows, or your team's tools are mainly Windows-based.

**All other job families (standard spec)**

- **MacBook Air M5** (Mac). Light and quick for everyday work.
- **HP EliteBook U5** (Windows). A reliable everyday Windows laptop.

Both models in a tier work for the same job, so pick the one you will be happier using. IT@LBG sets up both types. Your journey only shows the two models you are entitled to. If you think you are in the wrong tier, ask your line manager.

### Mobile phone

A work mobile phone (example: a standard smartphone) is available if your role needs one. Your line manager confirms whether you get one. Ask them if you are not sure. You collect it with your laptop.

### Headset

A wired or Bluetooth headset (example) for Teams calls is available to everyone. You can pick it as a peripheral.

### Other peripherals (optional)

- One or two monitors
- Keyboard and mouse
- A docking station
- A laptop stand

Pick only what your role needs. Your line manager can help if you are not sure.

## What to do

1. Open **Choose your primary device** on your journey and pick one of your two laptop models.
2. Optionally open **Choose peripherals** and pick any extras. You can skip this.

After the deadline, ask your line manager if you need to change your choice.

You collect everything on Day 0. See the collect equipment guide.

title: Policies and benefits overview
summary: A quick guide to holidays, pay, pension, wellbeing and learning.
body:
## Policies and benefits overview

Every figure on this page is an example for this demo. None of it is LBG policy.

### Holidays

25 days' holiday a year, plus bank holidays (example). Holiday is pro rata in your first year (example). Book holiday in Workday.

### Pay and pay day

Pay day is the last working day of each month (example). Your payslip is in Workday. If you have a question about pay, ask P&P through the help page.

### Working hours and flexible working

You can ask for flexible working from day one (example). Talk to your LM about what would work for you and your team.

### Pension

You are automatically enrolled into the pension scheme (example). Your contribution rate is set in Workday.

### Health and wellbeing

An employee assistance helpline is available 24 hours a day (example). Details are on the intranet.

### Learning

You get a learning budget each year (example) and access to the learning hub.

### Full policies

Full policy documents are on the intranet at https://example.test/policies (placeholder link).

title: Pre-employment vetting (PEV) explained
summary: What vetting is, what each First Advantage status means and who to contact if something goes wrong.
body:
## What is PEV?

Pre-employment vetting (PEV) is a set of checks we run before you can start. They confirm your identity, your right to work and your background, in line with the rules for the role (example).

Your personal details and check results are held in First Advantage, not in this app. This app shows your status and links you to the right place.

## What to do

1. Open First Advantage from the vetting task on your journey (https://example.test/firstadvantage, placeholder link).
2. Complete every step listed there. Give full and accurate information.
3. Upload documents only through First Advantage.

## What each status means

- **Not started:** the checks have not begun.
- **In progress:** checks are underway. You don't need to do anything.
- **Action needed:** we need something from you. Check First Advantage today. You will get reminders until it is done.
- **Cleared:** checks are complete. Your journey moves on.
- **Failed:** the checks could not be completed. P&P will contact you directly.

## If something is wrong

Contact P&P using the Teams chat link on this page. Don't send documents by email, and don't put personal details in chat. Use First Advantage or any secure link P&P gives you.

title: Set up your password and Microsoft Authenticator
summary: Step-by-step guide to set your password and add Authenticator before Day 1.
body:
## Before you start

You need your username from the welcome email (example). You can do this on your phone. You don't need your laptop yet.

## Steps

1. Open the password set-up link from the task: https://example.test/password-setup (placeholder link).
2. Enter your username.
3. Create a password. It must meet the rules shown on screen. Don't reuse a password from another account.
4. Install **Microsoft Authenticator** from your phone's app store.
5. On the set-up page, choose **Add sign-in method**, then **Authenticator app**.
6. Scan the QR code with Authenticator. Type the 6-digit code it shows.
7. Approve the test sign-in prompt on your phone.
8. Come back to your journey and tick the task off.

## Tips

- Never share your password, even with IT.
- Don't take a screenshot of your password or QR code.
- If you get stuck, raise an IT request or contact IT@LBG (https://example.test/it-help, placeholder).

Your LM can see if this task is still open a few days before your start date, so please do it early.

title: IT@LBG requests explained
summary: What you can ask IT for before you start, and how to raise a request.
body:
## What are IT requests?

IT requests ask IT@LBG for the access and software a starter needs for their role, such as shared drives or team tools (examples).

## When can I raise them?

Your line manager raises IT requests for you. They unlock once your Colleague File ID exists (created automatically by SailPoint). Your buddy can also help complete them.

## How to raise one

1. Your line manager (or your buddy) opens the IT request task.
2. Choose what you need from the list.
3. Add a short reason. Don't include passwords or personal details.
4. Submit.

## Tracking

Each request shows as Submitted, In progress or Done.

Your LM may also add team-specific requests, such as code repository access, from your team checklist.

## Need help?

Use IT@LBG self-service at https://example.test/it-help (placeholder link).

title: Eptura Engage: booking desks and meeting rooms
summary: Eptura Engage is the tool we use to book desks and meeting rooms. Your access is set up before your first day.
body:
## Eptura Engage

Eptura Engage is how colleagues book a desk or a meeting room in our offices.

### When you get access

Access is set up automatically once your internal account exists, before your first day. Your journey shows the status of this task.

### Booking your first desk

1. Sign in to Eptura Engage with your LBG account (link: https://example.test/eptura-engage).
2. Choose your office and the day you're coming in, for example your anchor days.
3. Pick a desk near your team. Your line manager can tell you which area they sit in.
4. Check in when you arrive.

### Meeting rooms

You can book a meeting room in the same way. Add the Teams link to the invite so remote colleagues can join.

If your access isn't working by your first day, ask your line manager or raise it with P&P.

title: Your photo ID pass: photo rules and steps
summary: How to upload a photo for your pass, what the photo check looks for and where the pass goes.
body:
## How it works

1. Upload a photo in the photo ID task.
2. The photo check runs straight away.
3. If the photo passes, your pass is ordered to your Day 0 location.
4. If it doesn't pass, you see what to fix. Take a new photo and upload it again.

## Photo rules

- Look straight at the camera.
- Your face must be clear and fully visible. No blur, no heavy shadows.
- Use a plain, light background if you can.
- No sunglasses.
- No hats or caps.
- Only you in the photo.
- Taken in the last 6 months (example).
- JPEG or PNG, under 5 MB (example).

## Head coverings

If you wear a head covering for religious or medical reasons, speak to P&P before you upload. Don't let the photo check decide this for you. P&P can review the photo and override the check.

## If the check fails

The check tells you what to fix. Try again. If you are still stuck, ask P&P through the Teams chat link. P&P can review and override the check.

## Your photo

Your photo is used only for your pass (example). It is sent to the pass supplier and is not kept in this app (example).

title: Mandatory training
summary: The courses you must complete, where to find them and what the status means.
body:
## What is mandatory training?

Mandatory training is a set of courses everyone at LBG must complete (example). The list comes from Workday, and your journey shows the same list with live status.

## Examples of courses

- Information security awareness (example)
- Data protection (example)
- Health and safety (example)

## Deadline

Complete all courses within 30 days of your start date (example).

## Status

- **Not started:** you have not opened the course.
- **In progress:** you have started it.
- **Complete:** you have finished it.

Status can take a day to update after you finish a course (example).

## Tip

Book a quiet hour in your calendar for the first two courses. They are the longest.

title: Team calls and Teams links (for LMs)
summary: How to forward or add your team's recurring calls and list the Teams links.
body:
## For line managers

The starter should join your team's recurring calls from their start date.

## Steps

1. List every recurring team call, such as stand-ups, team meetings and show-and-tells.
2. Forward or add each invite to the starter's calendar.
3. Add each Teams link to the list on the checklist (optional).
4. Tick the checkbox on the task.

## Tips

- Check time zones before you forward an invite.
- Tell the starter which calls are optional in their first week (example).
- Don't paste personal details into the link list. Team links only.

title: Book your Welcome to Lloyds induction
summary: The monthly induction run by P&P, and how to book a session.
body:
## What is it?

The Welcome to Lloyds induction is a monthly session run by P&P. It covers how LBG works, your first few weeks and who to ask for help. Sessions run monthly, online and in person (example).

## How to book

1. Open the induction booking task.
2. Pick a session from the list.
3. Confirm. A calendar invite is sent to you (example).

You can book sessions in your first month (example).

## Missed the booking?

If you have not booked by Day 0, a fallback task appears on your Day 0 journey. Book a session from there.

title: Order your home working items
summary: How to order a desk, chair, monitor and other home working items.
body:
## What you can order

You can order a set of home working items (example list):

- Desk
- Chair
- Monitor
- Keyboard and mouse
- Footrest

## Steps

1. Check the list above.
2. Open the home working order task.
3. Choose items and quantities.
4. Check the delivery address. It is the one on your records (example).
5. Submit.

Deliveries take about 5 working days (example).

## Something not on the list?

Ask your LM before you order it.

title: Flex benefits
summary: How to review and choose your flex benefits, and the deadline.
body:
## What are flex benefits?

Flex benefits let you choose extras from a menu, for example extra holiday, health cover or a cycle-to-work scheme (examples).

## How to choose

1. Open the flex benefits task. It links to the benefits platform (https://example.test/benefits, placeholder).
2. Sign in with your work account.
3. Review the options.
4. Make your choices and save.

## Deadline

Make your choices within 14 days of your start date (example).

## Missed the deadline?

Contact P&P through the Teams chat link on the help page. Don't wait until the deadline to ask.

title: Collect your equipment
summary: What to collect, where to collect it and what to bring.
body:
## What you collect

- Your laptop (the exact model you chose: MacBook Pro M5 Pro, MacBook Air M5, HP EliteBook U7 or HP EliteBook U5)
- The peripherals you picked, such as monitors, keyboard, mouse, dock or headset

Your journey lists the exact items.

## Where

The tech bar, Floor 1, Example House (example). Open 9:00 to 16:00 (example). Deliveries go to the mailroom on the ground floor.

## What to bring

- Your photo ID pass, or other photo ID (example)
- Your phone, with your journey open

## Steps

1. Show your pass at the tech bar.
2. Check the items against the list on your journey.
3. Sign for them (example).
4. Tick the task off in your journey.

## Something missing or damaged?

Tell the tech bar straight away, then let P&P know through the Teams chat link.

title: Check-ins with your LM
summary: How regular check-ins work and how to join one on Teams.
body:
## What is a check-in?

A check-in is a short, regular chat with your LM. It is a chance to share progress, raise concerns and plan the next few weeks.

## How often?

Your LM agrees the cadence with you. For example, weekly for the first month, then fortnightly (example).

## Joining

Each check-in has a Teams meeting link in your journey. Join from your phone or laptop.

## What to bring

- One thing that went well
- One question
- One thing you'd like help with

## Need to move one?

Message your LM on Teams. Don't just skip it.

title: Your 30-60-90 day goals
summary: How to write your first goals with your LM, and how to edit them together.
body:
## The three stages

- **Day 30:** learn the basics, such as tools, people and how the team works.
- **Day 60:** contribute to your team's work.
- **Day 90:** own a piece of work from start to finish.

## Example goals

- Day 30: set up my tools and meet my key contacts (example)
- Day 60: take part in one sprint or project (example)
- Day 90: lead a small piece of work (example)

## Steps

1. Draft your goals in the task. Keep to three per stage.
2. Share the list with your LM.
3. Your LM edits or agrees the list with you.

You and your LM can both see and edit the list. The task is done when you both agree.

title: Performance goals
summary: How performance goals work, and how your LM's goals cascade to you.
body:
## What are performance goals?

Performance goals describe what good work looks like in your role. They link your work to your team and business area.

## Cascaded goals

Your LM adds goals from your team and business area to your list. These show how your work fits into bigger priorities (example).

## Your part

1. Read the goals your LM has added.
2. Write any questions in the goal notes.
3. Agree the list with your LM.

## What this page does not cover

This page explains setup only. For how performance is rated, see the performance process on the intranet (example).

title: Development goals
summary: How to set development goals for your next steps, with your LM.
body:
## What are development goals?

Development goals are about the skills you want to build. For example, learning a new tool, taking a course or trying a stretch task (examples).

## Choose one to three

For each goal, note:

- **What** you want to learn or do
- **Why** it matters to you or your team
- **How** you will know you have done it
- **By when**

## Learning resources

The learning hub has courses and reading lists (https://example.test/learning, placeholder link).

## Finish this task

When you have shared your development goals with your LM, mark this task done. It is one of the Day 30 tasks that completes your journey.

title: Day one: what to bring
summary: A short list of what to bring and what to expect on your first day.
body:
## What to bring

- Your photo ID pass, once it is ready (example)
- Your phone, with the journey app installed
- A notebook (optional)
- Lunch, if you like (there are places nearby)

## Timing

Your LM confirms your meeting time and place. They show on your journey.

## What to expect

1. Meet your LM at the meeting point.
2. Say hello to your team and your buddy.
3. Collect your equipment from the tech bar.
4. Watch the executive welcome video.
5. Start drafting your 30-60-90 day goals.

Nothing on this list needs to be perfect. Ask questions freely.

title: Meet your team and your buddy
summary: Who is in your team, what your buddy does and how to say hello on Teams.
body:
## Your team

Your team page shows each member's role, photo and reporting line. Some members have a short bio. If a bio is missing, that is fine (example).

## Your buddy

Your buddy is a team member your LM picks for you. They are not your manager. Your buddy can help with everyday questions, such as where things are and how the team works.

Your journey shows your buddy's profile and a Teams chat link.

## Say hello

Use the Teams chat link to say hello before you start. A short message is enough, such as 'Looking forward to starting on the 7th'.

title: Signing in before you start
summary: How your guest invite works and how to sign in with your personal email.
body:
## Your invite

Before you start, you will get an invite by email to your personal address. Follow the link in the email.

## Signing in

1. Sign in with your personal email address.
2. You land on your journey.

Before you start you can see your journey, your team and your tasks. You will sign in with your internal account later, once it is set up.

## Can't find the invite?

Check your spam or junk folder first. If it's still missing, contact P&P through the help page and they can resend it.

## Use it on your phone

This app works in your phone's browser. You can add it to your home screen to use it like an app.

title: Who to contact for help
summary: Who to ask for help with each part of onboarding.
body:
## Who to ask

| Question | Who to contact | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your contract, pay, or your first weeks | Your LM | Teams chat |
| Vetting (PEV) | P&P onboarding team | Teams chat link on the PEV page |
| Passwords, laptop, IT access | IT@LBG self-service | https://example.test/it-help (placeholder) |
| Flex benefits | P&P | Teams chat link on the flex benefits page |
| Everyday team questions | Your buddy | Teams chat |
| Not sure who to ask | P&P onboarding team | Teams chat |

## The FAQ assistant

The FAQ assistant answers common questions from the onboarding content. If it can't answer, it offers to connect you to P&P.

title: Cloud Platform Engineering: your team checklist
summary: Team-specific steps for Cloud Platform Engineering: GCP project access, Google Cloud fundamentals training and the on-call rota briefing.
body:
## Welcome to Cloud Platform Engineering

These steps are only for colleagues joining Cloud Platform Engineering (example).

## Request GCP project access

Your line manager raises an IT request for access to the team's Google Cloud Platform projects (placeholder). It unlocks once your Colleague File ID exists. Access is read-only until you finish the fundamentals training.

## Google Cloud Platform fundamentals training

A short self-paced course (about four hours, example) covering projects, IAM, networking basics and billing. Find it in the learning hub (https://example.test/learning, placeholder). Mark the task done once you have finished it.

## Cloud on-call rota briefing

A 45-minute briefing run by the team (example). It explains the rota, how incidents are raised and who to call. You join the rota after your first month, not before.

## Questions?

Ask your buddy or your line manager.
